=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller's update and Disclosure Letter

**Scope:** I've reviewed only the Seller's update note and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA draft or the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Points on those documents rest on the Seller's own descriptions and should be checked against the source.

## 1. Overall read

The cover note calls these "key negotiated positions" and a "fair and balanced package". They are **Seller proposals, not agreed positions**, and our mark-up should say so.

The package is built so that the known problems cannot be recovered after Completion:

- **Clause 8.3** bars claims on anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.1-1.2** discloses the entire data room and public registers against all warranties.
- **The caps, basket and time limits** are then applied to everything, including title.

Together these mean that every issue we have found is both disclosed and excluded from claims. Those issues cannot be left to warranties. They need to be handled through conditions, price or funds flow, and specific indemnities that sit outside clauses 8.3, 12 and 20.5.

The Disclosure Letter is also more candid than the update note, and the two conflict:

| Topic | Update note | Disclosure Letter |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | Consent "addressed" | No final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions |
| Riverlark | Release after Completion | Facility not repaid, no discharge |
| Incident | "Not expected to be material" | Scope, access and notification are unknown |

Clause 1.4 says nothing is admitted, but these statements are still useful for negotiation.

## 2. Structural issues (the liability architecture)

**a) General disclosure and clause 8.3 (highest priority).** Disclosing the whole data room and public records, with constructive knowledge imputed to us, would neutralise the warranties.
- Require **specific disclosure only**, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. A reference to a data room folder is not enough.
- Delete clause 8.3. Replace it with an express **pro-sandbagging clause** saying the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge or investigations. The fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals, and it must never apply to indemnities or fundamental warranties.
- The disclosure date of 22 September 2026 is now stale. Require a **bring-down** of the disclosure at signing. Disclosures made after signing should not cure breaches and should only give a termination right.
- Disclosing "the Accounts" against warranties about the Accounts is circular and should be struck.

**b) Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 applying to "all Claims of any nature".** The same applies to the proposal that any limitation applies "unless expressly stated otherwise". This reverses the normal drafting position.
- Limitations should apply only to *General Warranty Claims* as defined.
- Carve out **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment**, specific indemnities, tax, fundamental warranties, and price-adjustment mechanics.
- The non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses must not exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct (Australian Consumer Law s 18 and Corporations Act s 1041H), and must preserve equitable remedies and termination rights.

**c) Cap, thresholds and time limits (cl 12.1-12.3).**
- **Cap:** AUD 4.8M (20%) is low, given that the quantifiable known items alone come to about AUD 4.1M (see section 3) before Bluefen and the incident. Counter at 30-50% for general warranties.
- **Basket:** AUD 250,000 (about 1%) as a deductible, where only the excess is recoverable, is Seller-favourable. Push for a **tipping basket** (full recovery once exceeded) at a lower figure. Reduce the de minimis from AUD 25,000, and allow related claims to be aggregated.
- **Time limit:** 18 months is workable for general warranties, but 24 months is better so that we get through a full audit cycle.

**d) Fundamental/title warranties.** The proposal to put capacity and title under the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" should be **rejected**. These should be capped at the **full purchase price**, with no basket or de minimis, and a long claim period (up to the 6-year contractual limitation period). The Seller's only evidence of title is the Company's own share register (DD-012), and the Disclosure Letter itself says the Buyer has not verified title. We should therefore:
- run ASIC and PPSR searches;
- review the constitution and the share transfer history;
- confirm that no Riverlark security covers the shares, or that it will be released;
- check for options or pre-emptive rights;
- take a full title, capacity and authority warranty.

**e) Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime", but they are not. Seek:
- a **pre-Completion tax indemnity** outside the caps and basket, with a claim period of at least the amendment period for assessments (4 years) and no limit for fraud or evasion;
- IP ownership warranties given extended cap and time protection, since IP is the core asset of an analytics business;
- confirmation of any R&D or other tax incentive positions, if the Company has claimed them.

**f) Seller covenant strength.** Harbourglass is a ventures holding vehicle and may distribute proceeds to its investors. Ask for a **retention or escrow** (for example 10-15% of price for 18-24 months) or a creditworthy guarantee. Otherwise any indemnity right is worth very little.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

| Issue | Seller position | Why it's a problem | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bluefen** (about AUD 3.6M, about 30% of revenue, implying about AUD 12M total revenue) | "Reasonable endeavours", consent satisfied on delivery of written consent | Consent not yet obtained (Disclosure Letter 2). Clause 11.3 conditions could make a "consent" worthless, for example if it imposes price cuts or termination rights. | Make it a **Buyer-benefit CP, waivable only by the Buyer**, requiring consent that is unconditional or on terms satisfactory to the Buyer, with the cl 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied. Add a long-stop date and a termination right. Seller bears any consent cost. If waived, use a price retention. |
| **Riverlark** (about AUD 3.2M) | Release "following Completion" | This is a debt-free deal, and the facility has change-control (cl 8.1) risk. A post-Completion release leaves security over the Company's assets in our hands. | Require a **payoff letter** with an exact figure (interest, fees and break costs). Pay it from the purchase price at Completion, with discharge documents (PPSR and any guarantees or share security) delivered **simultaneously**. |
| **Employee bonuses** (AUD 420,000) | "A matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, and the Disclosure Letter says they are *not* in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed and are extra. | Treat as a **debt-like item/transaction cost**: deduct from price or have the Seller fund it, including on-costs. Because of the continued-employment conditions, align this with retention planning. |
| **Ironquay IP** (AUD 180,000 open) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment | Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*. If the fee is unpaid, the Company may not own materials it uses, and it faces infringement and re-development risk. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified as unpaid. | Make payment, a receipt and a **confirmatory IP assignment** a CP. Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of title to or use of the materials, outside the caps. Add a warranty that all other SOWs are fully paid and assigned. |
| **DD-006 data incident** (about 1,240 records) | "Preliminary operational matter, not material" | Whether anyone accessed the file, the scope and the notification obligations are all unknown. The Company appears large enough to be covered by the Privacy Act (the small business exemption generally applies below AUD 3M turnover), so the **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme** is likely engaged. It requires an assessment within 30 days of suspicion. We do not know the discovery date, but the 30-day window may have lapsed. There may also be notification duties under customer contracts. | Do not accept "not material". Require: completed forensic findings (access logs, link expiry, recipient deletion confirmation), a statement of the Company's NDB assessment and any notifications made, and a **specific indemnity** for all losses, covering regulatory, customer and remediation costs, outside the caps and clause 8.3. |
| **Sandbar renewals** (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course" | The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued. Three identical amounts read together may point to a split contract. | Request the contracts, approval trail and any link to the Seller or related parties. Add **interim-period covenants** against new commitments without Buyer consent. Treat committed or unprovided amounts as debt-like or normalised working capital. |
| **Office lease and Mossvale** | Not material | The Seller's wording is only that these do not *state* consent is needed. That is not an assurance. | Review the clause text for deemed assignment on change of control. Take a specific warranty that no consent is needed, or add a CP. |

**Quantified known items:** Riverlark (AUD 3.2M), bonuses (AUD 0.42M, before on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 0.18M) and Sandbar (AUD 0.33M) total about **AUD 4.13M**. That is most of the proposed AUD 4.8M cap, and none of it is recoverable under the Seller's structure because it is all known. Bluefen and the incident come on top with no quantified figure. If the debt-like items go through price, the effective price falls to about AUD 20M, depending on the SPA's definitions of Debt and Transaction Costs, which I haven't seen.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Must-haves (gating):**
1. Reject general data room disclosure. Accept specific disclosure only, with a bring-down.
2. Delete clause 8.3 and add a pro-sandbagging clause.
3. Limit clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 to General Warranty Claims, and carve out fraud, indemnities, title and tax.
4. Make title and capacity a price-capped fundamental warranty with no basket and a long claim period.
5. Make Bluefen a Buyer-controlled CP, with a long-stop date and a retention fallback.
6. Require Riverlark repayment and discharge at Completion, paid from proceeds.
7. Pay the Ironquay SOW3 fee, obtain a confirmatory assignment as a CP, and widen the IP indemnity.
8. Obtain a data incident indemnity plus the forensic and NDB evidence.
9. Put the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs into the price or funds flow.
10. Add a tax indemnity.

**Negotiable commercial terms:**
- General cap: 30-50%.
- Tipping basket at a lower amount, and a lower de minimis.
- General warranty claim period: 24 months.
- Retention or escrow, or a guarantee.
- Sandbar: contract review plus an interim-period covenant.

**Diligence follow-ups:**
- Title searches (ASIC, PPSR).
- Full text of the Bluefen cl 11.2-11.3, lease and Mossvale provisions.
- Bluefen consent drafting.
- Incident discovery date and NDB assessment.
- Payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses.

**Process point:** respond expressly that none of the Seller's "negotiated positions" is agreed, and send the mark-up on a "subject to contract and ongoing due diligence" basis.

If useful, I can draft the mark-up language for the disclosure, knowledge, limitation carve-out and specific indemnity clauses next.
